subject: genetics
question: **Type:** application A researcher wants to watch the fate of every single cell during development of a living, transparent animal with a fixed cell lineage. Which model organism is best suited to this question?

options.text: Drosophila melanogaster, because it has giant chromosomes
Caenorhabditis elegans, because its transparent body and fixed cell lineage allow direct observation of cell fates
Mus musculus, because it is a mammal with physiology close to human physiology
Saccharomyces cerevisiae, because it grows as both haploid and diploid cells

explanation: Caenorhabditis elegans is transparent and has a fixed cell lineage, so every cell division can be observed in the living worm, which is how programmed cell death was first described in this organism. Drosophila melanogaster is used for its giant chromosomes and short generation time. Mus musculus is used for mammalian physiology and gene targeting. Saccharomyces cerevisiae is used for cell cycle control with its haploid and diploid life cycles.
